en: The Therāpadāna:
The Chapter on the Giver of Grass (Tiṇadāyakavagga), No. 8, The Apadāna of the Elder Bodhisammajjaka.
“In the past, I took up that Bodhi-leaf which had been discarded on the courtyard of the shrine and threw it away.”
I obtained twenty qualities.
By the power of that karma,
wandering through various states of existence,
I transmigrate through two states of existence:
among the gods and among humans.
Having passed away from the world of the gods,
Having come to human existence,
I am born into two families:
among the kshatriyas and also among the brahmins.
Endowed with all limbs and members, possessing the perfect proportions of height and girth,
I am handsome and pure.
With all limbs complete and no deficiency,
whether born in the world of the gods, among humans,
or wherever else one may be.
In existence, he is golden-hued,
like molten gold;
his skin is soft, supple, and smooth.
I was delicate and very tender;
my skin remained always so exceedingly soft even after I had attained enlightenment.
Wherever one goes among the realms of existence,
when the body has come into being,
the dust and mire do not stain it.
The karmic result ripens when the wings have fallen off;
whether from hot wind and sun,
or indeed from the heat of fire.
Sweat does not cease from the body;
this is the ripening of falling leaves.
There is leprosy, boils, and skin rashes.
Neither moles, nor pustules,
nor likewise itches appear on the body as a result of giving away a fallen leaf.
Furthermore, another quality arises for him in every state of existence:
no diseases occur in his body.
The karmic result ripens when the leaves have fallen away.
Furthermore, another virtue arises for him in every successive existence.
No mental distress arises as a result when one has discarded the leaves;
there is yet another virtue for him.
One is reborn in various states of existence;
yet for such a person, there are no enemies,
for the fruit of their actions has fallen away.
Furthermore, another quality arises for him in birth after birth:
he becomes one whose wealth is never deficient.
The maturation [of this] is like that of a leaf-fall.
Furthermore, another quality arises for him in every state of existence.
There is no fear of water from fires, kings, or thieves; furthermore,
there is another quality of his.
One is reborn in various states of existence;
female and male slaves become one's attendants,
following the dictates of the mind.
In whatever measure of lifespan one is born into human existence,
from that point on, their life does not diminish.
He remains for as long as his lifespan lasts.
[The people] both inside and outside, those from the towns and the provinces;
All are devoted to me,
desiring my prosperity and wishing for my happiness:
"May I become possessed of wealth and possessed of fame."
Possessing glory and supported by my kinsmen,
may I exist free from fear and terror in every state of existence.
Gods, humans, asuras,
gandhabbas, yakkhas, and rakkhasas—
all of them protect him.
Constantly wandering through existence,
having experienced both types of glory among the devas and among humans;
And at the end, he attained the auspicious, unsurpassed Nibbāna,
having dedicated it to the Fully Enlightened One.
Or even the enlightenment of that Teacher—
whatever merit a person may produce,
what indeed is difficult for them to obtain?
Having become superior to others in regard to the paths, fruits,
and future attainments, as well as in the qualities of meditative absorption and direct knowledge,
I am extinguished, free from taints.
Having joyfully cast aside what I had previously attained at the Bodhi tree, I am now at peace.
May I always be endowed with these twenty factors;
my defilements have been consumed by fire.
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) [have been attained].
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Bodhisammajjaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Bodhisammajjaka is the eighth.
